paper_metadata.title: The enhancement of tensile strength and elongation in two phase (NiAl+Ni3Al) intermetallics of Zr-doped Ni-20Al-27.5Fe (at.%) alloys

evidence.quote: Microstructure and tensile properties in the nickel intermetallics, Ni-20Al-27.5Fe and Ni-20Al-27.5Fe-1Ti (at.%), were investigated in order to understand the effect of zirconium addition.

attributes.location: phase boundary between NiAl and Ni3Al

evidence.quote: the chemical composition of the thin layer compound along phase boundary (C region in Fig. 2) is 59Ni-10Al-15Fe-16Zr in atomic percent.
These precipitates were identified to be Ni3Al phases within NiAl matrix, and NiAl phases within Ni3Al matrix, respectively, anlaysed by TEM diffraction in Choe's work [8].
The zirconium-doped alloy exhibits a thin layer along the phase boundary as shown in Fig. 1b, whereas the zirconium-free alloy does not show this feature.
The matrix phase of zirconium-doped alloy exhibits a mixture of subgrains as shown in Fig. 6a.
The compressive deformation caused by hot extrusion results in the fine precipitates within matrix phase, and they are precipitated more finely in zirconium-doped alloy than in zirconium-free alloy.
SEM-mapping for examining the zirconium distribution (Fig. 3) shows that the majority of added zirconium diffused into the thin layer region at the phase boundary.

The substructural observation conducted in the matrix phase reveals a large number of dislocations in most of grains, thereby indicating that many dislocation sources were activated during compressive deformation by extrusion.
The two-step hot extrusion has influence on increasing tensile strength up to 1350 Mpa at room temperature and keeping it high up to 600 Mpa at 700 °C.
The two-step hot extrusion has influence on increasing tensile strength up to 1350 Mpa at room temperature and keeping it high up to 600 Mpa at 700 °C.
The extruded specimens of zirconium-doped alloy exhibited a high tensile elongation of above 10% at all of test temperatures.

Tensile fracture strength and strain at room and high temperatures increased with zirconium addition owing to the enhanced grain boundary cracking resistance of the soft thin layers, in which much zirconium is segregated.
It seems that the zirconium segregated thin layer at the phase boundary brought about a microstructure refinement by recrystallization and precipitation within matrix grains during hot extrusion
It is believed that the fine structure of subgrains and precipitates improve tensile properties.
